jobs.description:
仿真场景搭建与资产配置:基于 NVIDIA Isaac Sim、Newton(Palatial/MuJoCo)等仿真平台,负责数字孪生场景搭建、机器人(如双臂机械臂、复合移动机器人)及物体的物理/渲染属性(USD、MJCF、Mass、Inertia、Bounds、CoACD 碰撞分解)配置与优化。
 抓取与操纵逻辑开发:负责物体抓取(Grasp Pose)、逆运动学(IK)、接触物理(Contact/Friction/Restitution)以及状态机(State Machine)逻辑的编写与测试。
 行为脚本与任务规划:编写基于 Python 的自动化行为脚本(Harness/Task Pipeline),实现“接近-抓取-抬起-振动/扰动测试-放置”等复杂离散/连续行为动作的逻辑控制与闭环校验。
 验证与指标分析:构建仿真测评 Pipeline(Metrics System),输出抓取成功率、滑移量(Contact Slide)、接触力等评估数据,并基于测试结果反向迭代 IK 与 Grasp 参数。
 算法协同与交付:与具身智能(Embodied AI)算法团队合作,为强化学习(RL)、模仿学习(Imitation Learning)或大模型部署提供高保真、稳定高并发的仿真环境与数据集生成接口。
 Real2Sim 与 Demo 生成:将第一人称视角(egocentric)等各类数据转化为高质量的 real2sim2real 仿真,用于数据集生成与 Demo 制作。
requirements: 计算机、机器人学、自动化、机电一体化等相关专业,本科及以上学历。
1 年及以上具身智能(Embodied AI)、机械臂抓取操纵或机器人仿真相关行业工作经验。
项目经验须体现机械臂抓取、灵巧手或接触操纵(manipulation)方向;仅有导航/SLAM/无人机/自动驾驶仿真经验、无操作类项目者不匹配。
精通 NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Omniverse) 或 Newton / MuJoCo 仿真框架,熟悉 USD / MJCF 物理描述文件结构。
熟悉仿真物理引擎机制(刚体动力学、接触力学、碰撞网格分解、CCD等)。
精通 Python,具备扎实的数据结构与软件工程规范,能够熟练编写面向对象的复杂逻辑脚本与自动化框架。
熟悉机器人学基础(空间变换、正/逆运动学 IK、碰撞检测算法)。
熟悉 Linux 深度开发环境、Git 版本控制与虚拟环境管理(venv / conda)。
具备严谨的调试与测试思维,能够独立追踪解决物理穿透、发散、接触抖动等仿真异常现象。
5. 英语能口头与书面沟通,能阅读英文技术文档
有 Palatial Newton、Isaac Gym 或 Brax 等高性能/并行仿真器实际项目经验者优先。
熟悉 ROS / ROS 2,具备硬件真机(如 UR、Franka、Yam 机械臂)部署或仿真到真机(Sim2Real)经验者优先。

1、熟悉伺服产品应用场景,专注通用伺服驱动器控制算法研究和迭代。 
2、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品响应速度、控制精度及工况适配性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
3、负责伺服三环(位置环、速度环、电流)控制算法优化,针对超调、震荡、低速抖动、高速响应滞后、稳态误差大、负载适应性差等都有切实的落地改良方案。 
4、对参数自辨识、死区补偿、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、高频振动抑制、低频抖动消除、弱磁控制、抗负责扰动观测、自适应PID、前馈控制等高性能算法都有深刻的理解,并能独立完成设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
5、跟踪先进伺服控制技术,结合公司产品定位,将新技术转化为量产可用方案,推动产品性能迭代升级。 
任职资格: 
1、硕士及以上学历,3年以上伺服(永磁同步电机)控制算法开发经验。 
2、有伺服三环(位置、速度、电流)控制算法优化落地应用经验,对伺服常见问题如速度超调/震荡、低速抖动、响应滞后、鲁棒性差等有优化经验。 
3、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品跟踪精度和鲁棒性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
4、对伺服速度控制高性能算法如机械/电气参数辨识、扰动观测器、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、振动抑制(高频共振和末端残余振动)、PID参数自适应等有实际开发经验,能独立完成算法设计、仿真设计、代码实现和调试闭环。 
5、对伺服电流控制高性能算法如弱磁控制、MTPA、模型预测控制、电流解耦等高性能算法有深刻的理解,并能独立完成算法设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
6、有伺服驱动器产品量产化应用经验优先。 
7、具有较强的软件调试能力,具备一定抗压能力。

jobs.description:
1. 负责机器人及机械臂端侧软件系统的全流程开发、调试与迭代维护,保障实机运行的稳定性与作业执行效率。
2. 落地机械臂运动控制、任务调度及智能控制算法的开发与验证工作,持续优化机械臂在抓取、装配、插拔等复杂操作场景下的作业精度与抗干扰能力。 
3. 推进强化学习、模仿学习等前沿算法在机器人实体操作任务中的工程化落地,完成算法从仿真环境到真实机械臂的迁移适配与效果调优。 
4. 联动感知、硬件、算法团队完成机器人感知、控制、决策模块的系统集成与跨设备联调,打通从模型训练到实机执行的完整交付链路。 
5. 快速定位并解决机器人现场运行中出现的软件缺陷、控制偏差及算法适配问题,沉淀技术解决方案与工程化规范,提升团队研发效率。
requirements: 1. 硕士及以上学历,计算机、自动化、机器人、机械电子、控制工程等相关专业,具备扎实的控制理论与软件工程基础。
2. 熟练掌握Linux开发环境,具备Linux环境下软件模块开发、调试及复杂问题排查能力;精通Python或C++至少一门编程语言,能独立完成功能模块的编码实现与性能优化。
3. 掌握机械臂运动学、动力学与控制相关基础理论,具备机械臂实机开发或调试经验,有力控机械臂实际操作与应用经验者优先。
4. 熟悉深度强化学习与模仿学习相关算法原理,了解SAC、PPO等在线强化学习方法及IQL等离线强化学习方法,掌握Behavior Cloning、Diffusion Policy等模仿学习方案,具备相关算法实际项目落地经验。
5. 了解VLA等机器人智能决策控制方案,熟悉LLM大模型微调(LoRA、DPO等)相关技术,了解视觉、雷达、触觉传感器等机器人环境感知技术原理。
6. 熟练使用ROS/ROS 2、MoveIt等机器人开发框架,掌握PyTorch、Isaac Sim、Isaac Lab、MuJoCo等深度学习与仿真工具;有强化学习/模仿学习算法在真实机械臂上的部署调试经验,或VLA、具身智能、大模型与机器人结合相关项目经验者优先。

西湖交互机器科技(杭州)有限公司,孵化自西湖大学跨力学实验室(Beyond Mechanics with Societal Impact Lab),是国内物理 AI 与商用具身智能机器人领域的前沿科创企业。 区别于传统纯数据驱动的数字化人工智能,公司以力学客观规律作为算法底层约束,融合智能感知与实时决策算法,让实体智能设备适配复杂物理工况,实现高安全性、可解释化落地作业。 依托实验室顶尖科研积淀,公司聚焦力学仿真、柔性材料、柔性感知三大核心研发方向,已在柔性机器人、自然人机交互取得关键性技术突破与产业化进展,其柔性机械臂实现“刚柔并济”突破,打破传统刚性机器人瓶颈,可完成复杂操作,提升人机协作安全性与适配性,填补行业空白。 当前公司为B端用户打造高阶机器人产品矩阵及定制化解决方案,深度落地特种作业、工业、医疗、康养等垂类场景,推动科研成果规模化应用,致力于成为全球具身智能机器人领域的技术引领者与场景落地标杆。

jobs.title: 具身智能大模型技术研究-阿里星-阿里巴巴2027届实习生_阿里巴巴集团校招_牛客网
jobs.description: 近年来,大型模型(包括大型语言模型(LLMs)、视觉-语言模型(VLMs)和扩散模型(DMs))的突破性进展,为高级感知、抽象推理和生成建模带来了前所未有的能力。这些进步为赋予机器人更类人的智能和适应性提供了变革性机遇。尽管取得了显著进展,当前的具身智能大模型在现实世界部署时仍面临诸多限制。一个主要挑战是它们难以泛化到新任务、未见物体和动态环境。这通常源于缺乏固有的常识性判断和对物理世界的精确理解,而这些对于应对物理现实的不可预测性至关重要 。因此,开发新一代具身智能大模型,能够自主学习、适应并以人类水平的熟练度、安全性和多功能性执行复杂的开放世界操作任务。 1. 围绕具身智能中的计算机视觉、机器人学、强化学习、自然语言等人工智能问题开展研究。 2. 推动具身智能领域的技术落地,研究机械臂、轮式机器人、人形机器人等具身智能机器人的运动/感知/控制/规划/交互算法,包括但不限于具身机器人的物体操纵、移动抓取、移动导航等算法和三维物体或场景建模理解等算法,实现室内外复杂场景下具身智能机器人自主任务执行。 3. 参与机器人领域相关多模态大模型的构建,负责具身机器人的复杂任务规划,主动环境感知理解与交互,技能学习与控制等前沿算法研究,研发具有感知-控制-规划能力的具身智能大模型。
requirements: 1. 具有机器人的控制、规划、感知算法的研究经验,熟悉深度学习,计算机视觉,多模态算法,机器人决策规划控制领域的前沿研究。 2. 极佳的工程实现能力,熟练掌握C/C++、Java、Python等至少一门语言。 3. 具备较强学习能力,对新事物保有好奇心,并能快速适应新环境;良好的沟通能力和团队协同能力;能与他人合作,共同完成目标;对所在领域有热情,不惧困难与挑战,善于独立思考并反思总结。 4. 加分项: 1)有ACM/NOI/IOI、Kaggle、国内外数学大赛、机器学习、深度学习相关竞赛获奖者优先。 2)在国际知名期刊或会议(NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR,ICRA,IROS,CoRL,RSS,CVPR,ICCV,ECCV等)上发表过高水平论文者优先。 3)有多轴机械臂、足式机器人等机器人平台算法研发及工程经验者优先。

二、模型二次开发与功能迭代 
1. 根据生产、销售、技术、质量、设备、经营管理等需求,对第三方搭建的产业大模型进行二次开发、接口改造和功能扩展。 
2. 参与Prompt工程、工作流编排、RAG知识库构建、模型微调和效果调优,提升模型在行业场景中的准确率和实用性。 
3. 开展AI应用脚本开发、接口调用、页面配置和简单后端开发,提高系统适配性和交付效率。 
三、AI应用落地与业务对接 
1. 推动大模型在生产调度、质量管控、成本核算、设备运维、客户技术服务、经营分析等场景落地应用。 
2. 对接各业务部门,梳理AI需求,输出可落地的AI应用方案、功能原型、实施计划及评价指标。 
3. 协同业务部门梳理流程、标准和知识规则,推动AI能力嵌入现有管理流程和业务系统。 
四、系统集成与接口开发 
1. 负责AI大模型与ERP、MES、WMS、OA、设备物联网平台等系统的接口对接、数据互通和联调测试。 
2. 编写接口文档、部署说明、运维手册和操作指引,形成标准化AI应用交付流程。 
3. 配合完成日志管理、访问控制、备份恢复和运行巡检,提升系统可靠性和可维护性。 
五、AI项目管理与成果沉淀 
1. 跟进AI项目进度,协调第三方厂商、内部IT和业务部门完成需求确认、开发联调、测试验收和正式上线。 
2. 建立应用台账、案例库和数据指标看板,沉淀AI场景、优化经验和复用组件,逐步形成公司内部AI能力体系。 
3. 开展用户培训、推广辅导和使用支持,提升员工使用率、应用覆盖率和实际业务价值。 
六、安全与合规管理 
1. 负责模型数据安全、权限管理、敏感信息脱敏和合规审查,确保AI应用符合公司信息安全要求。 
2. 对不符合业务需求、数据质量或安全规范的模型方案和上线版本提出整改建议或暂缓上线建议。 
3. 完成上级交办的其他与AI应用建设、运维和推广相关工作。

jobs.description:
实习证明 C/C++助教线下教育
工作内容 
1. 回复学员在学习过程中遇到的技术问题,协助分析并解决代码、软件环境、硬件接线及设备调试等问题。 
2. 完成部分课程内容的讲解,包括基础知识讲解、代码演示、实验操作和项目指导。 
3. 根据课程安排,提前熟悉课程内容、代码和硬件设备,做好课程讲解前的准备。 
4. 协助学员完成课程实验和项目,针对学员遇到的问题进行耐心指导。 
5. 对课程中经常出现的技术问题进行整理,形成常见问题说明或解决方案。 
6. 协助测试课程代码、教学案例和硬件设备,及时反馈发现的问题。 
7. 根据实际情况,协助整理课程资料、示例代码和操作文档。 
8. 配合完成其他与课程教学、技术答疑相关的工作。 
基础要求 
1. 具备一定的C语言基础,能够看懂和修改基础代码。 
2. 具备一定的Python基础,能够完成简单程序编写和基础报错排查。 
3. 了解数字电路、模拟电路相关基础知识。 
4. 能够看懂基础电路图、模块接线图和引脚说明。 
5. 有焊接、接线、电子元器件安装或硬件调试经验。 
6. 对机器人、嵌入式、人工智能、具身智能等方向感兴趣。 
7. 具备较强的学习能力,愿意主动学习没有接触过的新知识。 
8. 遇到问题能够主动查资料、测试和分析,不依赖他人直接给出答案。 
9. 具备一定的语言表达和讲解能力,能够将基础技术知识清楚地讲解给学员。 
10. 有耐心,能够根据不同学员的基础调整讲解方式。 
能力与态度要求 
1. 做事认真、细心,具备较强的责任感。 
2. 有主动思考和主动解决问题的意识。 
3. 遇到不会的内容时愿意主动学习,而不是直接放弃。 
4. 能够独立分析基础技术问题。 
5. 具备一定的逻辑思维能力和问题排查能力。 
6. 有较好的时间观念,能够按时完成安排的事项。 
7. 情绪稳定,能够耐心面对重复性问题。 
8. 能够长期、稳定地参与相关工作。 
9. 对技术有一定兴趣,愿意持续积累和提升。 
10. 不要求目前掌握全部技术,但需要有较强的学习意愿和执行能力。 
11. 回复问题及时,能够持续跟进问题,避免只回复一次后没有后续。 
12. 具备良好的沟通能力和团队协作意识。 
具备以下经验者优先: 
1. 有ESP32、STM32、Arduino等单片机开发经验。 
2. 有机器人、小车、机械臂等相关项目经验。 
3. 使用过编码电机、电机驱动、传感器或IMU。 
4. 接触过ROS2。 
5. 熟悉Linux或Ubuntu基础操作。 
6. 有PyBullet、Gazebo等机器人仿真软件使用经验。 
7. 参加过电子设计、机器人、智能车等相关竞赛。 
8. 有课程助教、教学、技术支持或社群答疑经验。 
9. 有技术文档编写、教程整理或项目复盘经验。 
10. 有可以展示的代码、项目、作品或比赛经历。

工作职责 
1.技术路线与架构规划 
定义物流人形 VLA 整体技术架构:视觉感知、多模态理解、自然语言任务指令解析、动作生成、全身运动控制、抓取操作闭环;制定 1-3 年物流场景 VLA 技术演进路线。 
2.VLA 模型研发与场景适配 
主导物流专属 VLA 大模型预训练、微调、RLHF / 模仿学习、强化学习落地;针对料箱、纸箱、包裹、不规则货物、货架、托盘做物体识别、姿态估计、6DoF 抓取、场景语义理解、环境动态避障。 
3.物流数据集与仿真平台建设 
搭建物流人形机器人多模态数据集采集、标注、清洗、迭代闭环;基于 Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 搭建物流仓储仿真环境,推进 Sim2Real 迁移,大幅降低真机调试成本。 
4.真机落地与工程化 
主导 VLA 算法与人形本体、运动控制、整机固件、调度系统、仓储 WMS/AGV 系统联调;解决真实仓储光照变化、货物堆叠遮挡、地面不平整、人员混行等复杂工况鲁棒性问题,保证高频稳定作业。 
5.团队管理与跨部门协同 
组建并管理 VLA / 具身智能算法团队,负责招聘、技术攻关、里程碑交付;对接产品、硬件、结构、电控、产线、物流客户,定义场景需求、算法指标、交付标准。 
6.前沿技术引入与专利壁垒 
跟进世界模型、具身大模型、端到端 VLA、扩散策略等前沿,快速落地到物流作业场景;主导技术专利、软著、顶会论文布局。
requirements: 1.硬性要求:计算机科学、人工智能、机器人学、自动化、控制工程、计算机视觉等相关专业博士学历(海外顶尖高校博士优先)。
2.工作经验:3 年以上 VLA / 具身智能 / 人形机器人算法研发经验(含博士期间课题研究及博士后经历),有物流仓储、分拣、抓取、码垛、工业搬运场景算法落地经验者优先。
3.博士期间深耕 VLA 多模态学习、具身智能、强化学习 / 模仿学习等方向,有相关顶会(NeurIPS/ICML/ICRA/IROS/CVPR)论文发表或核心专利产出;
4.精通视觉 - 语言 - 动作多模态架构,熟悉 OpenVLA/RT-2/GR00T/π?等主流人形 VLA 框架,熟练运用 PyTorch/TensorFlow 进行大模型微调与优化;
5.精通机器人 3D 视觉技术(点云处理、深度估计、6DoF 姿态估计、物体检测分割),熟悉 ROS/ROS2、Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 仿真平台及真机部署全流程;
6.具备扎实的数学建模与算法推导能力,能独立攻克物流场景下 VLA 核心技术难题(如杂乱货物抓取、动态避障、Sim2Real 迁移)。

主导过物流场景人形机器人 / VLA 算法从原型到量产落地项目。

| 我们正在基于可交互的 3D 仿真场景研发面向具身智能的世界模型。该岗位重点研究机器人动作与环境状态变化之间的关系,使模型能够从视觉、语言、机器人状态和动作序列中学习环境动力学,预测未来观测与状态,并服务于机器人规划、策略学习、数据生成和仿真到现实迁移。该岗位不是单纯的视频生成或 3D 场景制作岗位。候选人需要关注模型是否理解动作因果、物体持久性、空间关系、接触与交互结果,并建立能够衡量这些能力的训练和评测方法。## 工作职责- 基于厨房、客厅、商店等可交互 3D 仿真场景,构建世界模型训练与评测 pipeline。- 研究 action-conditioned video prediction、latent dynamics model、state-space model、video diffusion 和 autoregressive world model 等方法。- 融合 RGB、深度、点云、语义、机器人本体状态、动作、语言指令和物体状态等多模态信息。- 训练模型预测未来图像、3D 状态、物体轨迹、接触事件、奖励、成功概率或终止状态。- 利用仿真器生成大规模、可控且带有完整 ground truth 的交互轨迹,包括成功、失败、扰动和反事实数据。- 研究具有 3D 一致性、时间一致性、物体持久性和长时序记忆能力的世界表示。- 将世界模型用于机器人行为想象、model predictive control、策略规划、数据增强、奖励建模或策略预训练。- 设计世界模型 benchmark,评估视觉质量之外的动作可控性、动力学准确性、空间一致性、长期预测和下游任务收益。- 分析模型在遮挡、碰撞、物体状态变化、未见场景和未见动作组合上的失败模式与泛化能力。- 开发分布式训练、数据加载、实验管理、模型评测和可视化工具,提高研究迭代效率。- 与 3D 资产工程师协作扩展视觉与物体多样性,与机器人仿真工程师协作定义交互数据、状态标签和评测任务。- 跟踪并复现世界模型、视频生成、具身智能和 model-based reinforcement learning 的前沿工作,参与论文与开源项目。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python 和 PyTorch,能够独立完成模型训练、数据处理、实验设计和结果分析。- 理解 transformer、diffusion model、flow matching、VAE 或其他生成模型的基本原理。- 理解序列建模、表示学习、条件生成或动力学建模中的至少一个方向。- 具备机器人学习或 3D 视觉基础,理解观测、状态、动作、轨迹、坐标系和相机等概念。- 能够将研究问题转化为明确的数据协议、模型目标、消融实验和量化评测指标。- 具备较强的论文阅读、模型复现、工程调试和独立研究能力。## 加分项- 有 world model、video prediction、video generation、model-based RL、imagination-based planning 或 neural simulator 相关经验。- 熟悉 Dreamer、TD-MPC、MuZero、V-JEPA、Genie、GAIA 或同类世界模型工作。- 熟悉 Diffusion Transformer、Video Transformer、state-space model、tokeni

jobs.description: 1.负责具身智能领域的核心算法研究,包括但不限于多模态感知大模型(VLM/VLA)、强化学习(RL)、模仿学习、机器人运动规划与控制等; 2.研发具有“感知-规划-执行”一体化能力的具身智能大模型,实现机器人在室内外复杂场景下的物体操纵、移动导航、主动环境理解与人机交互; 3.将研究成果转化为实际生产力,解决具身智能机器人在实际任务中的长尾问题,完成从算法预研到硬件平台部署的全流程闭环; 4.紧跟国际SOTA(业界最先进)技术发展,持续推动技术创新,并在真实业务场景(如智能交通、机器人服务、工业协作等)中验证价值。
requirements: 1.本科及以上学历,计算机、人工智能、软件工程、数学、自动化等相关专业优先; 2.具备扎实的数学、算法和编程功底,熟练掌握 Python 或 C/C++; 3.深入理解深度学习原理,熟练使用 PyTorch、TensorFlow、JAX 等至少一种框架; 4.在计算机视觉、自然语言处理、机器人决策规划、控制理论、强化学习等一个或多个领域有深入研究或项目经验; 5.具备跨学科协作意识,能够与工程、硬件团队高效沟通,共同推进目标达成; 6.对具身智能领域充满热情,具备强大的自驱力和抗压能力。 【加分项】 1.论文成果:在国际顶级期刊或会议(如CVPR, ICCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS等)以第一作者发表过高质量论文; 2.竞赛获奖:在ACM-ICPC/NOI、Kaggle、国内外顶尖数学/机器人大赛中取得优异成绩; 3.有过实际机器人硬件平台(如多轴机械臂、足式/人形机器人、轮式底盘)的算法研发或工程化经验,熟悉ROS/ROS2等中间件; 4.开源贡献:在 GitHub 拥有高质量开源项目,或在相关开源社区具有影响力。

jobs.description:
1、负责双足机器人运动控制与步态算法的设计、开发和优化。 
2、负责人形机器人双手操作与全身运动(locomotion)的智能控制策略开发,针对复杂场景(如重物搬运、精准拆码垛、行走、爬楼梯、障碍物跨越等)实现操作与运动的全身协调。 
3、基于深度强化学习、模仿学习等方法优化运动策略,提升机器人在动态环境中的自适应能力与运动效率。 
4、负责算法从仿真到实机的迁移部署,开发在线动力学参数辨识与自适应校准方案,解决 sim2real gap 问题,保障真机运行的实时性与稳定性。 
5、建立算法鲁棒性评估机制,通过扰动测试验证运动策略在真实场景中的可靠性。 
6、跟踪运动控制领域前沿技术,持续进行算法创新与性能优化。
requirements: 1. 精通机器人运动学、多刚体动力学建模与求解,1 年及以上人形机器人/机械臂具身项目开发经验
2. 精通 PyTorch/Jax 等深度学习框架,熟悉 Diffusion/Flow matching 类算法,有完整的 Diffusion/Flow Matching 类算法的开发优化经验。
3. 熟练掌握至少一种主流的 Diffusion 或者 Flow Matching 强化学习后训练算法(DPPO,Flow-SAC, Flow-GRPO), 有完整的实践和开发经验。
4. 掌握 IsaacLab、MuJoCo 等至少一种强化学习仿真环境开发
5. 熟悉 lerobot, RLinf, SimpleVLA-RL 等至少一种动作扩散模型强化学习后训练框架,有实际的开发落地经验优先。
6. 熟悉 PI0.5,GR00T,OpenVLA 等 VLA 模型优先
7. 熟悉人在环真机强化学习算法(HIL-Serl,Conrft),有实际的人在环真机数据收集框架开发者优先

| 我们正在建设面向具身智能的仿真训练与真实场景执行系统。该岗位的最终目标不是只在仿真中获得较高成功率,而是让机器人进入真实的商店、客厅、厨房等场景,安全、稳定地完成导航、抓取、放置、整理和人与机器人协作等任务。该岗位负责打通从仿真场景、任务与数据构建,到策略训练、真机集成、现场调试和真实任务评测的完整链路。候选人需要具备良好的机器人系统与 Python 工程能力,能够定位感知、规划、控制、通信、硬件和环境之间的系统性问题,并对机器人在真实场景中的最终执行结果负责。## 工作职责- 在 RoboCasa、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill、robosuite 或其他平台中搭建机器人仿真场景。- 将 3D 资产转换并配置为 USD、URDF、MJCF 等仿真格式,完成尺度、坐标系、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节和物理属性设置。- 根据真实商店、客厅、厨房等目标环境构建数字化场景,配置机器人、相机、光照、传感器和可操作物体,并控制仿真与实景之间的关键差异。- 设计具身智能任务,明确 instruction、initial state、action space、success condition、failure condition、reset distribution 和 benchmark split。- 为模仿学习、强化学习、Diffusion Policy、ACT、VLA 和 LeRobot 等训练流程生成、清洗和管理轨迹数据。- 将仿真或数据训练得到的策略部署到真实机器人,完成模型转换、推理服务、机器人接口、传感器接入和控制链路集成。- 在真实场景中完成机器人标定、定位、导航、抓取与操作调试,包括相机内外参、手眼标定、坐标系、末端执行器和动作精度校准。- 设计并实施 sim-to-real 方案,包括域随机化、系统辨识、真实数据回采、策略微调和仿真参数校准。- 组织真实机器人任务测试,建立现场部署、任务初始化、失败恢复、人工接管、日志回传和重复实验流程。- 分析真机失败案例,区分感知、规划、控制、通信、策略、硬件和场景因素,并推动问题闭环。- 为真实环境中的人员、设备和物体制定安全约束,落实速度与力限制、碰撞保护、急停、工作空间限制和异常降级机制。- 开发自动化场景与任务检查工具,检测穿模、碰撞体错误、动力学异常、不可达、不可抓取、任务无法重置和成功判定失效等问题。- 建立贯通仿真与真机的可复现训练和评测 pipeline,对比成功率、碰撞率、恢复率、任务耗时、泛化能力和 sim-to-real gap。- 设计场景、物体、初始状态和语言指令的随机化方案,并控制训练集、验证集和测试集之间的泛化难度。- 使用 Codex 等 Agent 工具辅助代码开发、批量实验、数据清洗、结果分析和失败案例归因。- 与生成式 AI Agent 与 3D 资产工程师协作定义资产接入标准,与世界模型研究工程师协作定义交互数据和策略接口。- 参与机器人学习、sim-to-real、真实场景部署和 benchmark 方向的创新研究与论文工作。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python,能够独立完成仿真环境、数据处理、实验脚本和自动化工具开发。- 理解机器人学基础,包括坐标变换、位姿、运动学、轨迹、碰撞检测、传感器和控制等概念。- 具有真实机器人开发或实验经验,能够进行设备连接、标定、动作调试、日志分析和故障排查。- 熟悉 Linux 环境,能够使用 ROS 或 ROS 2 完成机器人、传感器和算法模块之间的集成。- 了解机器人操作、导航、模仿学习或强化学习中的至少一个方向,并理解从模型输出到真实机器人动作执行的完整链路。- 理解 mesh、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节、材质、相机和尺度等仿真资产概念。- 能够定义清晰、可执行、可自动评测的机器人任务,并将同一任务协议落实到仿真和真实环境。- 具备较强的问题拆解、现场调试和工程执行能力,愿意参与真实场景搭建、真机实验和迭代部署。## 加分项- 熟悉 MuJoCo、RoboCasa、robosuite、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill 或 Habitat 中的一个或多个平台。- 熟悉 imitation learning、reinforcement learning、Diffus

articles.title: 短期降温不改长期趋势,具身智能投资更看重赛道前景与企业成长潜力-36氪
articles.summary:
### 行业热度:融资金额回落,资金更关注可验证的经营进展
融资降温尚不等于资金全面退出,需求明确、经营进展可验证的项目更有说服力。第一财经据IT桔子事件库梳理,7—9月披露融资额分别为86.54亿元、175.41亿元和71.50亿元,9月较8月下降59.2%;地瓜机器人、苏度科技等仍获十亿元级融资。该报季后采访也显示,部分机构更关注真实订单与现金可支撑时长。
### 政策驱动:政策支持延续,地方布局更强调产业适配与使用成效
政策支持延续,地方布局更强调产业适配、真实需求与使用成效。8月28日,国家发展改革委既支持实训场、中试基地及数据、模型、标准建设,也强调围绕真实场景、真实需求推进应用。9月国家数据局座谈会延续这一方向。支持创新与约束盲目投入并行,地方不仅要比较招商数量和建设规模,更需说明本地有什么客户、配套与运营条件。
### 技术驱动:陌生环境作业能力改善,可靠性与经济性决定落地速度 [...] 融资降温与应用扩展在同一季度发生。9月披露融资额低于7月和8月,但仍有十亿元级融资;9月10日,国家数据局继续支持企业增加数据投入,强调科学布局。9月24日,智元与长隆宣布首期部署超过300台机器人,覆盖演艺、导览等场景。资本趋于审慎,应用探索并未停止。局部投入和估值过热的风险值得警惕,仍须逐项检验交易、使用成效与回报条件。
## 二、六维证据指向短期调整,真实需求与技术进步仍支撑长期发展
综合研判:短期调整预期与投入节奏,长期机会取决于需求兑现和企业能力
六维证据支持“短期降温不改长期趋势”:资本与政策要求投入更加审慎,技术、销售和应用又提供了持续发展的依据。当前更接近预期、交易质量与投入节奏的阶段性校正,尚不足以据此判断产业需求全面收缩;调整持续多久,仍取决于后续技术和经营进展。
长期增长也不会平均分配给所有赛道和企业。需求强度、技术门槛、成本收益与竞争结构决定赛道空间;产品复用、稳定交付和客户经营决定企业能否获得增长;交易价格则决定增长能否转化为投资回报。
以下从行业热度、政策驱动、技术驱动、市场规模、客户需求与商业化进程六个维度,分别说明上述判断的证据与边界。

articles.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
articles.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baseline

articles.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations

articles.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
articles.summary: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. articles.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
articles.summary: When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable. A view that is informative for one task can be useless for another, even at the same workstation. We introduce Seeing What Matters, a benchmark for task-conditioned actionable spatial belief in simulated tabletop manipulation. Across three domains--coffee workstation, drawer/cabinet, and microwave/appliance--the benchmark provides 860 frozen evaluation cases; expanding across methods, budgets, and inference repeats yields more than 115,000 evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization. articles.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
articles.summary: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurati

articles.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have become a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, but their effectiveness still depends heavily on large volumes of demonstration data. In manipulation tasks, this dependence is compounded by structured spatiotemporal uncertainty in the action space: multiple nearby actions or trajectories may successfully solve the same task, while semantically equivalent demonstrations often unfold at different speeds. Standard pointwise supervision treats each demonstrated action as an exact target, imposing an unnecessary learning burden under such uncertainty. We present SURE, a data-efficient VLA training framework that explicitly models both spatial and temporal uncertainty. SURE augments a VLA backbone with a lightweight transposed-convolutional probabilistic action decoder that captures spatial uncertainty through local correlations among neighboring action bins. It further introduces Soft-DTW alignment supervision to accommodate local timing

articles.title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, organizing continuous robot execution into separately predicted segments and thus introducing potential discontinuities at action-chunk transitions. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action-chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. Given visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioceptive information, ODEAction learns an action transition field defined over action space, where a transition vector characterizes the evolution rate of the current action with respect to evolution time. During execution, the model takes the current action as its initial condition and integrates the learned field using an ordinary differential equation (ODE), recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as an action head and does not depend on a specific vision-language backbone architecture. Experiments on LIBERO, EBen

articles.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
articles.summary: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. articles.title: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
Horizon-Coupled Obstacle Guidance for Relative-Action Diffusion Policies
articles.summary: Real-world robot deployment requires adapting learned policies to unseen obstacles without collecting new demonstrations or retraining. Existing policy-level guidance often applies obstacle corrections independently at individual horizon steps, which may address local obstacle violations but fail to coordinate the action sequence into a complete, task-directed detour. How obstacle responses should be propagated across the action horizon to coordinate complete, task-directed avoidance motion remains underexplored. We introduce an inferencetime obstacle-guidance framework for pretrained relative-action diffusion policies. It rolls out cumulative relative actions into a workspace trajectory, evaluates obstacle interactions along the trajectory with an SDF-based obstacle model, and propagates each obstacle response to all contributing action increments during denoising. articles.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning
articles.summary: Recently, world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for robot manipulation. By jointly modeling action generation and future observation prediction, WAMs can act and anticipate the outcomes of the actions. However, existing WAMs typically rely on frozen pretrained encoders trained with reconstruction, which may not produce representations well suited for robot control. In this paper, we tackle the problem of learning physicallygrounded, control-relevant representations for WAMs. We propose MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone. While naive joint training can lead to feature collapse, MDF++ introduces a multi-task learning strategy that leverages cross-modal correlations to learn task-relevant representations. articles.title: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References
articles.summary: Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design. We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions. To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks. articles.title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning
articles.summary: Robot policies trained on visually narrow demonstrations can become sensitive to environmental features that are unrelated to the task. Existing generative augmentation methods can introduce visual diversity, but processing every frame and camera view independently is computationally expensive and may produce inconsistent observations across cameras and timestamps. We introduce Augmentron, a geometry-aware pipeline that generates reusable scene representations and renders them through recorded camera poses. This produces temporally and multi-view consistent environ- ment and workspace variations while preserving the robot, task objects, actions, and annotations. Across three physical manipulation tasks, replacing half of the real world training dataset with Augmentron data improves model success across three tasks for both in out-of-distribution distractor objects, and out-of-distribution workspace variation evaluations. articles.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
articles.summary: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. articles.title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking
articles.summary: Language-guided embodied person tracking requires a mobile agent to identify a target from a referring description and consistently follow the target under egocentric observations. We present DobotTrack, a target-grounded vision-language-action (VLA) framework that integrates auxiliary grounding supervision with efficient temporal modeling. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. We introduce Q-identity, a target-conditioned historical visual compression module that leverages target-grounding predictions to selectively preserve identity-discriminative appearance features and spatial cues in compact historical tokens. On EVT-Bench, our 0.8B-parameter model achieves an average success rate of 77.9%, exceeding OmTrackVLA by 16.9 p

articles.title: ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use
articles.summary:
Creative tool use is a fundamental human capability and an important step toward general-purpose embodied intelligence. It requires agents to reason about object affordances, physical constraints, and manipulation strategies, especially when standard tools are unavailable. However, progress in this area is limited by the lack of real-world datasets that capture human tool-use behavior with sufficient scale, fidelity, and diversity. Existing benchmarks are often simulation-based, focus on simplified interactions, or lack detailed observations and annotations.
 We introduce ToolDex, a large-scale egocentric-exocentric (ego-exo) human demonstration dataset for creative physical tool use. ToolDex captures scenarios in which humans select, adapt, and repurpose available objects as tools. Using synchronized egocentric cameras and eight exocentric cameras, the dataset provides high-fidelity multi-view observations and rich annotations for hands, tools, target objects, and their deformable int

articles.title: A Controlled Study of Models, Skills, Feedback, and Curriculum in Agentic Robotics
articles.summary: Agentic robotics asks coding agents to implement and iteratively improve robot policies from simulated and real-world physical interactions. We study the self-learning loop of agentic robotics through a controlled simulation study spanning nine manipulation tasks, 631 different experiment configurations, and 28K coding agent rollouts, systematically varying model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum. The experiment data suggests that the bottleneck is often not the access to sufficient information, but interpreting it into the right policy update. Across these factors, a successful self-learning loop depends on how effectively agents attribute failures, reason task-relevant spatial and geometric structure, and selectively restructure code to improve policies.

articles.title: FASTFUNNELS: Agile Multi Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces via Adaptive Dynamic Funnels
articles.summary: We focus on the problem of high-speed multi-robot navigation in cluttered spaces with tight spatial constraints. A key challenge is balancing safety with agility, as existing methods often trade one for the other (slowing down near a bottleneck to avoid collisions versus failing to swerve in time at high speeds), especially for car-like systems. Our approach belongs to the family of formation control methods, in which Ackermann-steering agents coordinate while navigating tight spaces. However, current formation control techniques rely on rigid, pre-defined shapes and transitions that depend on initial conditions, the environment, and vehicle dynamics, and are impractical to maintain at high speeds. For example, agents passing through a small gap must first form a square, transform into a line using analytical equations, and then return to a square. articles.title: RevoSim: Scalable Multimodal Tactile Simulation for Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: We present RevoSim, a scalable and high-fidelity multimodal tactile simulator for the BrainCo Revo3 hand that jointly models 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips. RevoSim efficiently generates synchronized pressure, depth, RGB, and marker-displacement observations; on a single RTX 5090, its depth-conditioned marker-displacement configuration supports up to 4,096 parallel environments. We train in-hand manipulation and grasping policies entirely in simulation, establishing a foundation for future sim-to-real transfer. Project page: https://braincotech.github.io/RevoSim-web/.

articles.title: HOC2R: Hand-Object Contact Trajectories for Human-to-Robot Motion Transfer
articles.summary: Human videos contain abundant object-manipulation demonstrations, but they do not directly provide motion cues that a robot can follow. We present HOC2R, a Hand-Object Contact trajectory extractor for Robot motion that combines frozen DINOv3 and SAM 2.1 features with learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization. HOC2R supports two modes: count-aware automation that detects, counts, and localizes visible contacts in untrimmed videos, and fixed-two localization for two-finger grippers when contact frames are known. On a 30-task point-annotated benchmark, count-aware automation improves contact-count accuracy from 58.1% to 71.4% and reduces mean localization distance from 19.81 to 10.46 pixels relative to an adapted VRB2 baseline. On seven unseen RGB-D rollouts, a five-task fixed-two checkpoint reduces mean localization distance from 67.67 to 27.02 pixels. articles.title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models promise a single language-conditioned policy adaptable to many manipulation behaviors, yet deployment additionally requires skill retention and long-horizon composition: a policy must retain previously acquired skills and reuse them inside composite tasks whose behavior changes across phases. The standard recipe absorbs every new task into one shared update, which provides neither a parameter-level locus for reusable skills nor a mechanism for invoking each skill along the trajectory. We observe that this missing structure is latent rather than absent: per-skill low-rank updates of a pretrained VLA occupy a robustly distinguishable, low-dimensional subspace, and a single composite-task LoRA concentrates roughly half of its Frobenius energy in this subspace, against a near-zero matched random-rotation control. articles.title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety
articles.summary: Recent progress in embodied robotics is bringing robots closer to deployment in homes, as vision-language models (VLMs) are demonstrating significant advances in reasoning, making VLM-driven robots promising home assistant agents. These agents will often be introduced into homes that already have cameras, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and residents with wearables. To fulfill their potential, they need to integrate with existing smart infrastructure and reason through ambiguous scenarios: a smoke alarm may come from a pan about to ignite, a pan already on fire, a resident cooking or a faulty sensor, and each calls for a different response. To that end, we introduce HomeLoop, a simulation framework and benchmark built on Isaac Sim that combines robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, simulated residents and visitors, faulty sensors, and hazards that evolve over time. articles.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes
articles.summary: In recent years, massively parallelized rigid-body simulation has played a central role in robotics research, enabling rapid progress in areas such as reinforcement learning, stochastic optimal control, and randomized smoothing-based trajectory optimization. Particularly in contact-rich settings, the scalability of such simulations in large part depends on well-optimized representations of collision geometry, often requiring a coarse approximation of the underlying surfaces using primitives such as spheres, capsules, cylinders, and boxes. Whenever the complexity of the surfaces or the precision demands of the application render such approximations insufficient, it is instead necessary to employ mesh-mesh collisions, which impose a significant reduction in throughput. This paper proposes a simulation framework designed from scratch to address this bottleneck, with novel routines for broadphase and narrowphase collision detection as well as the subsequent contact dynamics computation. articles.title: STRIDE: Learning Humanoid Locomotion in Minutes with Acceleration-Based Rewards
articles.summary: Learning locomotion directly on a humanoid robot is a promising direction to avoid the sim-to-real gap. However, locomotion rewards in Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically track the base velocity, which cannot be measured onboard without an external motion capture system or well-calibrated state estimator. This is why we introduce \method{}, which learns humanoid locomotion from minutes of samples with a reward that only requires the onboard Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). Instead of tracking the base velocity, STRIDE rewards the robot for following a commanded acceleration profile. To learn efficiently from this reward, we use the off-policy RL algorithm XQC and combine a high gain setting for the joint position controllers with left-right symmetry augmentation. In simulation, STRIDE learns to walk on the Unitree G1 and Booster T1 humanoids within 14 minutes of samples. articles.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation. We propose \ours, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action. The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations. articles.title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly
articles.summary: Geometric assembly requires fine spatiotemporal coordination to place parts without causing collisions or deadlocks under tight clearances. To address this, we present an object-centric reinforcement learning framework that treats each part as an agent and learns a shared policy for continuous assembly control. A graph neural network represents the pieces, their target poses, and their spatial relationships, and predicts translational and angular velocities for each component. Per-agent proximal policy optimization with a centralized graph critic directly learns motion and temporal coordination within a single feedback policy. We study this formulation through planar Tangram assembly, where pieces must slide and rotate into a given configuration while remaining on the assembly surface. Q11:WITA-OMNI(智元开发的端到端全模态交互大模型)为什么要统一语音、视觉、表情和动作?
熊彦:我们让所有模态回到原始阶段统一预训练,后补模态会造成智力损失,也难以对齐对话时机。人和人不是一问一答,而是用表情和肢体语言回应,天然是全双工交互,具身机器人还要用视觉判断“这句话是不是对我讲”。在长隆乐园里,小朋友声音小,机器人会主动打招呼、单膝跪地或弯腰,拉近交互距离,这是固定音箱和普通模型做不到的。

熊彦:第一是鲁棒性,任何一句话都接得住。比如,实景演示有约1秒混响,模型仍靠拒识能力扛住混淆声音。第二是情绪,理解情绪并给予情商回应,交互速度和智商在Preview阶段已走上正确路径。 [...] 姚卯青:它采用WRAM(World Reasoning Action Model)架构,训练重新做,同时在不同Check Point持续加数据。数据来源包括既有采集、觅蜂采购和补充渠道。既有高端双目数据,也有GoPro等单目低成本数据,目前训练集已超过百万小时。(编者注:GO-3 Preview是智元发布的全球首个实现预训练/后训练/部署后全链路规模化学习的具身模型。)

articles.title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: Recent advances in robot foundation models have highlighted the potential of in-context learning (ICL) for adapting robot behavior from demonstrations without further fine-tuning. Previous work has used retrieval-based post-training to equip pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models with the capability for ICL by teaching them to condition action predictions on retrieved visually-relevant demonstration chunks. However, the effectiveness of retrieval hinges on selecting context relevant to the current execution stage, which visual similarity alone may not capture. We introduce VICTR, a framework enabling in-context learning in VLAs via progress-informed context retrieval built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator (IC-VFE). articles.title: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing
articles.summary: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace. However, humanoid cart pushing remains challenging because the bimanual grasp closes a force-coupled loop in which the contact wrenches that drive the cart also disturb the robot's balance, and payload changes alter the coupled dynamics. We propose ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework that regulates cart velocity through two-stage reinforcement learning. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support. A force latent and a state latent are then inferred from onboard observations, without external force sensors, and fed to a residual policy that coordinates bounded arm, waist, and leg adjustments with base-velocity commands. articles.summary: We propose, HaNDF, object-conditional neural distance fields as data-driven priors for modeling the plausible hand-object configurations, in the product manifold of hand articulations. This makes it crucial to develop a generative prior which can model the plausible hand poses conditioned on the object under interaction. To this end, our HaNDF proposes a geometry-aware, object-conditioned neural distance field, representing the plausible articulations in the zero-level set of a conditional field. We leverage tools from Riemannian geometry to (i) represent plausible hands in the zero level-set of an object-induced neural field, and (ii) project a given pose onto this field. articles.summary: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments. A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training. We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency. articles.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. articles.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. articles.title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions
articles.summary: As robots are deployed in the real world, they will inevitably make mistakes. Human interventions provide valuable feedback for improving their behavior, enabling them to adapt online to new scenarios. However, studying human-in-the-loop robot learning is difficult: real-world experiments are slow and expensive, so most algorithm development relies on simulated human models. We show that common human modeling assumptions do not match how real people intervene in practice. Through analyzing intervention data from human participants, we find that humans tend to intervene when agent progress stalls, and that their corrective actions are often suboptimal. articles.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. articles.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
articles.summary: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. articles.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
articles.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes action prediction and alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and spatial representations from a frozen 3D perception model. articles.summary: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. Recent approaches use novel-view synthesis (NVS) to augment demonstrations with unseen viewpoints, but they assume static scenes and therefore fail to re-render the manipulated object during the post-contact interaction phase, leaving the most critical parts of the demonstration unaugmented. articles.summary: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. Existing methods use geometric rules or hard stability masks, limiting how risk can influence the joint choice of box, orientation, and placement. We propose Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (SHORE), which combines a learned stability probability of a placement with an on-policy estimate of its return conditional on stability. A 3D U-Net learns stability from executed outcomes and simulated alternatives, revealing outcomes of actions underrepresented in early rollouts. articles.summary: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. articles.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
articles.summary: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? articles.summary: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion. However, using 3D inputs at deployment requires additional sensing and processing, making image-based policies more practical. We ask whether an image-based policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while retaining a purely image-based interface at deployment. We propose shape-teacher alignment, a training-time mechanism that uses a pretrained 3D shape representation as an alignment target for an image-based policy encoder. articles.summary: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. articles.summary: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. articles.summary:

articles.summary: For perceptive humanoid locomotion, the relevance of terrain geometry depends on the robot's body state and how both evolve under its actions. articles.summary: We consider the problem of sequential task continuation, where one robot acts in a workspace that has been affected by a previous robot. articles.summary: We present a progressive imitation framework that learns terrain-appropriate humanoid parkour skills and subsequently adapts their hand--knee support. articles.title: HITCH: Teaching a Vision-Language Model to Operate a Humanoid through a Whole-Body Harness
articles.summary: Enabling vision-language models (VLMs) to control humanoid robots requires both reliable whole-body interfaces and knowledge of how to use the body that carries over across tasks. articles.title: Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning
articles.summary: Knowledge of the hidden interior structure of an object, including the presence and location of cavities, is essential for predictive simulation, robotic manipulation, and nondestructive inspection. articles.title: MessyNav: Zero-Shot Navigation via Manipulation in Messy Environments
articles.summary: Real-world environments are messy, with paths often blocked by everyday objects like chairs and toys, requiring robots to perform interactive navigation by manipulating obstacles to clear a path. ## 03 美国做AI,中国做硬件
Meta选择傅利叶,表明了中国机器人制造能力在全球产业链中的重要性。
傅利叶早期专注于外骨骼和康复机器人,随后进入人形机器人领域。其GR系列产品经过多代迭代,在双足运动、灵巧手和触觉感知等方面积累了研发经验。
傅利叶GR-3概念机器人宣传图
对于Meta来说,与已有产品和制造经验的企业合作,可以减少从机械结构、零部件到整机装配的摸索时间,将更多资源投入AI模型和交互系统。
中国企业的优势还体现在产业配套和实际应用场景上。人形机器人涉及电机、减速器、传感器、结构件和控制系统等多个环节,中国拥有较为完整的制造供应链,也有大量工厂和工业客户可以提供测试环境。
据外媒报道,2026年上半年,中国具身智能企业在322笔交易中获得935亿元融资,约合130亿美元,是去年同期的五倍。投资范围已经从整机制造延伸到机器人AI模型、训练数据和软件系统。
中国企业正在尝试解决机器人如何学习陌生任务的问题。 [...] 从研发人员驻场到中国供应链岗位招聘,Meta正在把机器人项目从单台原型机向更完整的研发和制造体系延伸。不过,目前尚无证据表明Meta已经确定量产计划或产品发布时间。
## 02 让Muse拥有“身体”
Meta研发Max,核心目标与其AI智能体Muse有关。
Meta首席技术官安德鲁·博斯沃思(Andrew Bosworth)曾在内部将人形机器人称为Muse的物理载体。这意味着Meta希望AI不仅能够通过对话回答问题,还能借助机器人在现实环境中执行任务。
今年5月,Meta收购了机器人AI初创公司Assured Robot Intelligence。这家公司专注于开发机器人模型,帮助机器理解人类行为,并适应不同环境。相关技术和团队也成为Meta机器人研发的一部分。
从现有布局看,Meta正在补齐机器人AI所需的软件能力,同时通过Max测试这些能力如何与硬件结合。 [...] 当AI开始进入物理世界,决定产品竞争力的将不只是模型有多聪明,还包括它能否通过一副可靠的身体,把理解转化为行动。对机器人产业而言,这比制造出一台能够行走的人形机器更难。

articles.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
articles.summary: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. articles.summary: Code-as-policy agents often use execution feedback to retry failed programs. articles.summary: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. articles.summary: Vision-based tactile sensors capture multiple aspects of physical interaction within a single image stream, including contact appearance, geometry, indentation depth, and tangential deformation. articles.summary:
Generalist robot policies are trained on static offline datasets, yet physical manipulation unfolds sequentially across stages. Because a weakness in a downstream stage remains unobservable until the policy passes earlier ones, each resolved bottleneck exposes the next hidden failure mode. This staged structure calls for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), in which a policy iteratively executes, diagnoses failures, and updates itself. Moreover, because task completion behaves like a product of stage-level pass rates, recursive gains can multiply across generations. articles.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
articles.summary: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI. By streaming visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, the framework enables users and embodied agents to interact with evolving virtual environments. It supports both predicting the visual consequences of actions and generating observations from physical state maintained by an external simulator. We demonstrate this approach across camera navigation and robot manipulation, controllable video transfer, and multi-view autonomous vehicle (AV) simulation. These examples provide a shared foundation for developing interactive virtual environments for Physical AI training and evaluation. Our code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos and https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples. articles.title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
articles.summary: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. articles.summary: In the real world, mobile manipulation robots must perform complex object interactions and make multi-step decisions, often relying on task-relevant information that is no longer observable. articles.summary: Ensuring safety in advanced robot control methods such as Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning remains an open challenge. articles.summary: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering information that is no longer visible, such as an object's location before occlusion or the order of a demonstrated action sequence. A large vision-language planner can read this history, but calling it before every action chunk is slow and costly. We present a three-tier system for the RoboMME benchmark. GPT-6 Astra (System 2) selects a grounded subtask from stored visual history, a $π_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy (System 1) executes it, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B monitor (System 1.5) checks after each action chunk whether the subtask is finished. The instruction is kept until the monitor reports completion or a task-specific event occurs, while the policy keeps acting on new observations. On RoboMME, the system succeeds in 79.13% of episodes with an average of 3.63 Astra calls and 80.84 seconds per episode. articles.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
articles.summary: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. articles.title: Online Adaptation to Latent Physical Properties for Learning from Demonstration
articles.summary: Manipulating visually identical objects with different physical properties requires adapting actions based on information acquired through interaction. We address the problem of learning from demonstrations how to adapt manipulation actions, such as regrasping and changing contact locations, based on physical-property information acquired during interaction.
